title: Parameters and Arguments
summary: Parameters are the named inputs a function accepts; arguments are the actual values you pass when calling it.
learningObjectives: Apply the concept in a small program
Predict program output by reading code

sections.content: Parameters are the named inputs a function accepts; arguments are the actual values you pass when calling it.
Functions can take zero, one, or many parameters. Order matters — the first argument fills the first parameter, and so on.
Key points: parameter names live only inside the function, and callers do not need to know the internal names — only the positions.
Summary: Parameters and Arguments — practice the example by changing values and predicting the output before running it.
